description:
## Objective and authorization
Implement the agreed channel attachment failure policy through the existing outgoing delivery path. The user authorized implementation, then the contract audit identified a lifecycle gap and work stopped under the user's no-drift rule. The user has now requested that the issue reflect the revised policy-option approach below. This update changes planning only; no implementation, commit or push is part of this update.

User constraints: preserve contract lifecycle and decoupling; prevent module leakage across boundaries; reuse current paths; no scope drift or speculative abstractions. If implementation requires deviation, STOP the affected work and report the concrete conflict, evidence, impact, and smallest alternative before proceeding. Do not silently add a workaround.

## Agreed behavior
- Read send_on_file_failure from the selected connector, default true when absent. Resolve a stable policy for the outgoing attempt. No attachment policy effects on ordinary text-only messages.
- On: after attachment failures, publish the message with successfully prepared/uploaded files and log failures; if no files succeed, publish text only when transport certainty permits.
- Off: if any required attachment fails before publication, do not publish the final message.
- Email: apply this decision to preparation outcomes before constructing/submitting one MIME email. SMTP has no independent remote attachment-upload stage; SMTP transport failure affects the whole submission.
- Mattermost: ZAQ selects the policy before calling the existing send/edit path. JidoChatBridge translates it into a provider-neutral option (semantics: continue or abort; finalize naming against existing conventions). The adapter uploads, enforces that supplied policy before publication, and reports the outcome through the existing return path. Successful uploads are reused without uploading them again. Control does not return to ZAQ between upload and publication.
- In strict/abort mode, complete all required uploads across all planned posts before publishing or updating the first post. Any known preparation/upload failure prevents final publication. Provider publication can still fail after earlier posts were accepted; report partial/uncertain outcomes without claiming atomicity.
- Policy support must be explicitly declared through the existing capability mechanism. edit_message/edit_attachments govern create-versus-update behavior and do not imply support for attachment-failure policy. Do not let an unsupported adapter silently ignore strict mode; detect unsupported policy before side effects and return a clear unsupported-policy result. Toggle visibility follows native file-send capability only, per the latest user correction. The attachment_failure_policy capability is a runtime enforcement check, not a visibility requirement.
- An uncertain final submission must not trigger automatic replacement sending. Preserve the existing no-resend contract. Already streamed text cannot be undone; already uploaded provider files may remain. Multiple post publication is not atomic.

## Contract and lifecycle guardrails
- ZAQ Channels owns policy selection from connector configuration. EmailBridge applies that policy to local preparation before SMTP submission. JidoChatBridge translates it into a provider-neutral send/edit option; the adapter executes the supplied policy using provider-owned upload facts. Bridges translate outcomes into the existing ZAQ delivery contracts.
- Provider upload behavior, limits, file IDs and per-file remote outcomes belong to ../jido_chat_mattermost. Do not build parallel provider upload tracking in ZAQ.
- Use the supported Jido boundary. Channels.Api must not invoke Mattermost modules or HTTP endpoints directly; the sibling adapter must not depend on ZAQ modules, structs, callbacks or configuration storage.
- Reuse/extend current Outgoing, DeliveryFiles, DeliveryError, bridge send/upsert, adapter send/edit and DeliveryConfirmation paths. No second outbound pipeline, duplicate materialization, callback-based orchestration framework, generic dispatcher, or automatic Action/tool exposure.
- Reuse/extend structured delivery results, including the existing adapter delivery_report, to distinguish uploaded files from published/confirmed files and retain failures and certainty. ZAQ consumes reporting rather than duplicating provider upload tracking.
- Preserve a single send/edit invocation and its current lifecycle. Upload references remain adapter-local for that invocation, bound to its connector, destination and operation; do not return a resumable upload plan to ZAQ. No new public upload/publish API, callback into ZAQ, cross-layer upload handle, persistent upload registry or retry framework.
- The adapter receives a policy value only, never a ZAQ module, struct, callback or configuration object. Confirm the SDK preserves the option and normalized result on existing post/send/edit routes. Make any necessary compatible capability/option extension at its owner; stop before introducing a separate lifecycle.
- Preserve routing, actor authorization, threading, create/update choice, streaming placeholder identity, reply-callback timing and confirmation lifecycle. Confirm only actually delivered files/posts, once; bookkeeping failure must not cause resending.
- Log safe identifiers, stage and sanitized reason; no file bytes, credentials, source handles or raw confidential errors.
- If the existing Jido contract cannot support this without a new cross-layer coupling or a lifecycle change, stop and report before implementing that change.

## Evidence and reuse assessment
Observed current owners:
- lib/zaq/channels/api.ex resolves delivery connection and orchestrates fallback/confirmation.
- lib/zaq/channels/delivery_files.ex prepares files using existing materialization/decoding; currently fails at the first error.
- lib/zaq/channels/email_bridge.ex and email_bridge/smtp_sender.ex prepare attachments before one SMTP submission.
- lib/zaq/channels/jido_chat_bridge.ex adapts prepared files and calls the Jido send/edit path.
- ../jido_chat_mattermost/lib/jido/chat/mattermost/adapter.ex uploads before each post, plans multiple posts, and already reports partial delivery through metadata.delivery_report.
- The sibling transport/req_client.ex uploads batches but currently returns an error without retaining earlier successful batch results if a later batch fails. The current multi-post loop can publish earlier parts before later uploads fail.
- Contract audit: Jido.Chat.Adapter exposes send_message, send_file, post_message and edit_message; it has no supported attachment upload-now/publish-later contract. Mattermost upload_files is private to its adapter. The earlier ZAQ-intermediate-decision design would therefore add a lifecycle boundary. That design is superseded by carrying a policy value through existing options and returning outcomes after the adapter completes its operation.

Decision: extend existing contracts and operation paths, not new standalone Actions. Shared preparation remains local transport adaptation; provider upload/publication stays adapter-owned. Reuse existing materialization and validated DecodeBase64 execution, NodeRouter event boundaries, send/edit operations and receipt recording.
Before implementation, verify current upstream interfaces, references and Action/tool consumers; refresh the reuse assessment if the code has moved. Preserve compatibility for other SDK/adapter consumers: define absent-option behavior and explicit support negotiation rather than changing all callers implicitly. No new public upload API is planned or authorized.

Related decisions: zaq-juu.17 (removed preparation callback; preserve direct prepare/3 composition), zaq-juu.18 (data-only delivery errors and ZAQ fallback/no-resend ownership), zaq-juu.11 and zaq-juu.16 (unified outgoing delivery and avoiding redundant validation). Review these before changing contracts.

## Implementation sequence
Decompose into dependency-linked child issues before coding, respecting repository planning policy:
1. Verify option propagation, capability declaration and result normalization across ZAQ, Jido and the sibling adapter. Define a compatible provider-neutral policy value and unsupported-policy behavior within existing contracts. Do not introduce a two-stage public API.
2. Extend Mattermost's existing send/edit options and internal upload/publication path to enforce the supplied policy, retain successful upload outcomes, and produce existing-style delivery reports. Strict mode uploads all planned files before the first publication. Validate within the sibling repository.
3. Extend shared preparation and email orchestration to retain usable files and apply the selected policy before SMTP submission, preserving materialization, authorization and one-email submission.
4. Wire configuration and policy support through existing Channels/Jido paths; ensure legacy fallback cannot override abort or cause a second send. Preserve receipt/callback behavior and finalize truthful capability-aware UI wording.
5. Validate contract compatibility, failure paths and complete journeys; update authoritative docs only as needed.

## Acceptance and verification
- Default/on/off behavior, missing settings, capability visibility, save/reopen and accurate email versus upload wording.
- No attachments, one file, partial failure and all-file failure; successful attachments keep identity/order and failures do not appear in confirmation.
- Preparation failure, upload rejection, partial batch upload, all uploads successful, and failure at final create/edit.
- Strict mode performs no final publication when an upload/preparation failure is known; all planned uploads, including later post groups, finish before the first final post/update.
- The policy value reaches the adapter through existing options on create and attachment-edit paths. Explicit capability support is checked; unsupported strict mode fails before side effects. Ordinary edit capability alone never implies policy support.
- No adapter callbacks into ZAQ, leaked provider modules, resumable cross-layer upload state, new send lifecycle or parallel outbound path.
- On/default mode preserves usable files and reports failures; off/abort mode suppresses preparation/upload fallback sending. Existing ZAQ fallback must not send a second message after the adapter has already handled the policy.
- Existing post/placeholder updates and multi-post partial publication remain correctly reported; no fabricated rollback guarantee.
- Timeout/exception before or after publication, no duplicate upload/send, and confirmation failure without resend.
- Test existing public execution paths using current dependency seams; preserve authorization and source files. Add property checks where invariants warrant them.
- Run repository mix q and isolated tests, sibling quality checks, then the applicable final precommit gate. Follow each repository's testing policies.
- Existing test behavior changes require explicit approval. Two existing ChannelsLive assertions currently expect Advanced settings hidden for file-capable channels without configurable upload size; approval to update those expectations is still pending.
- Assess feature E2E need; use the repository human UX approval gate if required.

## Current working-tree state
The Advanced settings panel has been moved below Enable. A default-on persisted UI switch and two new UI tests exist, but runtime policy enforcement is not implemented. Last UI validation: mix q passed, 74/76 tests passed; the two old visibility assertions conflict with the new setting. Recheck live state before starting; this issue is not a completion claim.
